title: Context is Key: A Benchmark for Forecasting with Essential Textual Information
authors_or_org: Andrew Robert Williams, Arjun Ashok, Étienne Marcotte, Valentina Zantedeschi, Jithendaraa Subramanian, Roland Riachi, James Requeima, Alexandre Lacoste, Irina Rish, Nicolas Chapados, Alexandre Drouin
supported_claim: Crafted essential context benefits several strong direct-prompt forecasters; large contextual numerical failures remain. Context-region-weighted scoring and clipping require care when transferring results.
limitations: Not enterprise AI spending; contextual relevance is constructed, not retrieved from a noisy company corpus; does not establish execution probabilities.
license_status: Article displays arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license; benchmark/code licenses not verified.

title: Rethinking Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting Evaluation
authors_or_org: Haoxin Liu, Yichen Zhou, Rajat Sen, B. Aditya Prakash, Abhimanyu Das
supported_claim: Real-world TimesX changes CiK method rankings; tested code revisions underperform components and simple averaging wins. It distinguishes announcement/occurrence dates and uses post-cutoff evaluation.
limitations: Public real-world series are not enterprise AI spend. Daily/weekly focus. Numerical-aware event selection needs separate deployment reproducibility assessment; paper leakage controls do not certify private product data.
license_status: Article displays CC BY 4.0; code and component dataset reuse licenses unverified.

title: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation
authors_or_org: Xu Liu, Hanshu Yan, Taha Aksu, Quang Pham, Zhongzheng Qiao, Jun Hao Liew, Silvio Savarese, Doyen Sahoo, Junnan Li; Salesforce AI Research
supported_claim: Structured effects derived from realized future improve numerical realization; explicitly excludes extraction/validation of raw-source future information; code editing can suppress local dynamics.
limitations: Oracle-like future effects and difficulty filtering; not an as-of extraction or enterprise forecasting demonstration; recent preprint.
license_status: Article displays CC BY 4.0; underlying datasets/code not independently license-checked.

title: Time-MMD: Multi-Domain Multimodal Dataset for Time Series Analysis
authors_or_org: Haoxin Liu, Shangqing Xu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Lingkai Kong, Harshavardhan Kamarthi, Aditya B. Sasanur, Megha Sharma, Jiaming Cui, Qingsong Wen, Chao Zhang, B. Aditya Prakash
published_or_version: arXiv:2406.08627v4, 2025-01-24; first submitted 2024-06-12; NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks
supported_claim: Multimodal features can help; prefix integration can hurt; embeddings and smaller text backbones deserve comparison rather than assuming LLM scale benefits.
limitations: Nine public domains; different task and collection process from private enterprise communications. Reported contamination protections are model/version dependent.
license_status: Article displays CC BY 4.0; Appendix V states dataset ODC-By v1.0. Underlying source rights and code licenses require separate inspection.

title: Are Language Models Actually Useful for Time Series Forecasting?
authors_or_org: Mingtian Tan, Mike A. Merrill, Vinayak Gupta, Tim Althoff, Thomas Hartvigsen
supported_claim: Removing or replacing language-model components in three investigated forecasting architectures did not reduce accuracy and often improved it.
limitations: Numerical architecture ablation does not prove genuinely new textual context is useless; results limited to evaluated methods/data.
license_status: Reuse license unverified; no code or data imported.

title: Effective forecasting and judgmental adjustments: An empirical evaluation and strategies for improvement in supply-chain planning
authors_or_org: Robert Fildes, Paul Goodwin, Michael Lawrence, Konstantinos Nikolopoulos
published_or_version: International Journal of Forecasting 25(1):3–23, January 2009; DOI 10.1016/j.ijforecast.2008.11.010
kind: primary empirical research; author institution record/abstract
supported_claim: Across over 60000 forecasts from four supply-chain firms, judgment improved averages in three firms; small adjustments often harmed accuracy and upward revisions helped less often.
limitations: Institutional abstract inspected, not full paper. Supply-chain demand does not determine AI-spend thresholds or bias patterns.
license_status: Reuse license unverified; bibliographic record/abstract used for research attribution only.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
authors_or_org: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang
published_or_version: arXiv:2307.03172v3, 2023-11-20; first submitted 2023-07-06; TACL accepted 2023 per arXiv
supported_claim: Tested language models show sensitivity to relevant information position in multi-document QA and key-value retrieval, even with long context windows.
limitations: Older model population and retrieval tasks; not a failure-rate estimate for current Factory models or enterprise event extraction.
license_status: Article reuse license unverified; author repository displays MIT but no repository material imported.

title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
authors_or_org: Miao Xiong, Zhiyuan Hu, Xinyang Lu, Yifei Li, Jie Fu, Junxian He, Bryan Hooi
supported_claim: Verbalized confidence can be overconfident; tested confidence techniques do not consistently dominate and struggle on challenging tasks.
limitations: Confidence in answers is distinct from event realization or spending distributions. Does not evaluate current enterprise models.
license_status: Reuse license unverified; no code or data imported.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
authors_or_org: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, Mario Fritz
supported_claim: Instructions placed in retrieved data can manipulate LLM-integrated application behavior and API calls; source content is not action authority.
limitations: Demonstrates a threat class on evaluated systems, not current product exploit frequency or complete mitigations.
